clue.text: Small cat almost longing to stand

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: almost says the word for longing stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: an ache is a longing or yearning

explanation.surface: A little cat, nearly pining, tries to stand up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last letter from ACHE, leaving ACH. 'stand' is the verb meaning tolerate, not a physical posture.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to put up with or tolerate it, which is what one can or cannot stomach.

clue.text: Anxiety as American's cut hair

indicators.note: cut means a letter is chopped off the American abbreviation

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for American
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Worry as an American has a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' looks like part of a haircut, but here it trims the American abbreviation down to its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental strain or tension, a near synonym of anxiety.

clue.text: Busy people

definitions.meaning: to busy someone is to keep them engaged
to people a place is to inhabit it

explanation.surface: Crowded with people.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to keep someone busy and to live in or fill a place, as people do.

clue.text: Fish initially eating dragonflies after adult very quietly drew near

indicators.note: after puts the fish behind the adult and very quiet letters

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings
PP is pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
a roach is a freshwater fish

indicators.note: initially says take the first letters of the words eating and dragonflies

explanation.surface: A fish crept quietly up, eating dragonflies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' looks like it puts one piece inside another, but it gives only its own first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Approached means came closer to something, which is to have drawn near.

clue.text: Will try to be on time

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: A determined effort to be punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' is the legal sense: a judge hears or tries a case.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart means courage or determination, the willpower to keep going.

clue.text: Cross after European squeeze, say

indicators.note: after places the cross letter behind the European letter in the answer

parts.note: a cross is drawn as the letter X
to press is to squeeze

explanation.surface: An angry continental gives a squeeze, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like the adjective meaning angry, but it is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to put it into words, which is to say it.

clue.text: Former lover criticises this writer over new increase in size

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
to pan is to criticise harshly
this writer means the setter, I
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: An ex slates the writer for putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Expansion is growth in size or extent, the act of getting bigger.

clue.text: Bucket washed out, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that the word sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: washed out means pale or faded

explanation.surface: A bucket faded from washing, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: A pail is an open container with a handle, another word for bucket.

clue.text: Finally fiddle books? Tax collectors see all!

indicators.note: finally says take the last letter of fiddle

parts.note: NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
IR is the Inland Revenue, the former UK tax authority
Ely is a cathedral city whose bishop's diocese is a see

explanation.surface: Cooking the books at last? The taxman sees everything!
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' and 'books' suggest fraudulent accounts; 'see' is a bishop's diocese, here Ely in Cambridgeshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Entirely means wholly or completely, as in all of it.

clue.text: Team respects how crabs move

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
respects as in 'in some respects' means ways

explanation.surface: A team honours the way crabs scuttle.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs famously scuttle laterally, moving to one side rather than forward.

clue.text: Go over river with speed, travelling west

indicators.note: in an across answer, travelling west means read from right to left, so the word for speed runs backwards

parts.note: pace means speed

explanation.surface: Crossing a river fast while heading westwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To recap is to summarise again, going over the main points of something already said.

clue.text: A page with purpose? Editor agreed

parts.note: the point of something is its purpose

explanation.surface: A page with a clear aim, and the editor signed it off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appointed, like an appointed time, has been fixed or agreed in advance.

clue.text: Keeping up in golf after two drinks

indicators.note: after puts the two drinks before the rest in the answer

parts.note: a sup is a small drink and port is a fortified wine, two drinks side by side
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Staying upright on the golf course after a couple of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporting something holds it up, the same as keeping it up.

clue.text: Conservative tier boast

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the UK political party
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A Tory in the upper tier brags.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag or gloat loudly, which is boasting.

clue.text: Nasty United Nations petitions want leader to be removed

parts.note: pleas are petitions or appeals

indicators.note: leader to be removed says the first letter of want is dropped

explanation.surface: Unpleasant UN appeals demand a leader be ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: Nasty and its synonym here both describe something disagreeable or offensive.

clue.text: Gathering everyone by yard from time to time

parts.note: an occasion is a social event or gathering
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone meets in the yard every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasionally and from time to time are synonyms meaning now and then.

clue.text: Mum's eaten nuts for fun

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of Mum's eaten go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Mother has eaten nuts just for the fun of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusement is entertainment or enjoyment, which is what fun is.

clue.text: Carved up coldest bananas leaving nothing

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters of up coldest are jumbled

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Chopping up the coldest bananas until none are left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' rearranges UP COLDEST once 'leaving nothing' takes out an O.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculpted describes something shaped by cutting, as a sculptor carves stone or wood.

clue.text: Swimming lesson includes introductions to requisite kids' breathing equipment

indicators.note: includes means the rearranged lesson letters hold the other letters inside them
swimming means moving freely, so the letters of lesson float into a new order
introductions to says take the first letters of requisite and kids'

explanation.surface: A swimming lesson features the gear children need for breathing underwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimming' makes SNOELS from LESSON; 'includes' puts R and K inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Snorkels are tubes that let a swimmer breathe with their face underwater.

clue.text: So cold, queen's only dancing to preserve temperature

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: to preserve means to hold safely inside, so the rearranged letters keep the temperature letter within them
dancing says the letters of the words queen's only move about into a new order

explanation.surface: It's freezing, so the queen keeps dancing to stay warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' makes ONSEQUENLY from QUEENS ONLY; 'to preserve' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: So, as a linking word, means therefore or as a result, the sense of consequently.

clue.text: Burns part of housing estate

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fire damages part of a housing estate.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to scorch slightly, a mild way of burning.

clue.text: Green reforms with unknown power

indicators.note: reforms means shapes anew, so the letters of Green are rearranged

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: Environmental reforms with an unknown source of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy is power, as in electricity supplied to homes.

clue.text: Angler might use this line by river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A fisherman casts his line by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A lure is a bait or fly an angler uses to attract fish.

clue.text: December talk: what we could hang on the tree

definitions.text: what we could hang on the tree

parts.note: an oration is a formal talk or speech

explanation.surface: A Christmas-time speech about trimming the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Baubles and tinsel hung on a Christmas tree are ornaments, each one an example of this.

clue.text: No warships regularly retreat

indicators.note: regularly says take every second letter of no warships

explanation.surface: No warships ever retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a peaceful refuge, figuratively a retreat from the world.

clue.text: Son leaves spread — and another?

indicators.note: leaves means the son letter departs from the word for spread

parts.note: paste is a spread for bread

explanation.surface: A boy abandons his sandwich spread for a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another?' points back to 'spread': the answer is also pâté, another spread, written here without its accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is a savoury meat or fish paste spread on toast, so it is another spread.

clue.text: Adolescents irregularly eat greens

indicators.note: irregularly says the letters of eat greens are put into no fixed order

explanation.surface: Young people seldom eat their vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescents are young people aged thirteen to nineteen, the years with -teen in them.

clue.text: Firework beginning to go off, creating fury

indicators.note: beginning to go off means the first letter of the firework word is dropped

parts.note: a banger is a loud firework in Britain

explanation.surface: A firework starting to explode makes someone furious.
explanation.walkthrough: A BANGER is a British firework that explodes with a loud bang; losing its first letter leaves the answer. 'go off' looks like the firework exploding.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is intense rage, a strong form of the same feeling.

clue.text: Norfolk town hospital department's lack of agreement

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, England
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A small-town hospital ward cannot agree on anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissent means disagreement or difference of opinion, so it is a lack of agreement.

clue.text: Please speak about this husbandless female

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for speak surrounds the rest

parts.note: to say is to speak

indicators.note: husbandless means the letter H, for husband, is removed

parts.note: taken as written before losing a letter

explanation.surface: A request to discuss this unmarried woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husbandless' drops the H, a standard abbreviation for husband; 'about' wraps the verb for speak around what remains plus F.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to content or gratify them, meeting their wishes.
